scope.sample: StockLedger / StockLedgerSnapshot projection apply-event kernel pure-function families with per-view business-semantics faces
scope.purpose: Independent small sample of the traditional family-26 artifact under the semantics-face shape: per view the generator emits (1) the kernel pure-function class (@Singleton @Inject() with one function per judged event, four forms, delegating every business-semantic hook through the injected face), (2) the per-view semantics trait (the business question face: emptyRow / stamped / text), and (3) the bootstrap module binding face to impl. The handwritten impls (infrastructure.projection isolation zone, generator never creates or overwrites) own the view's business defaults — the empty row, the named untimestamped timestamp default (epoch0/null -> now, the single sanctioned clock read), and the text default. Two views pin the full construct set: StockLedgerView exercises create/updateOnlyx4/delete with all three hooks plus the kernel-local upsertBy pure mechanic; StockLedgerSnapshotView exercises persistenceIdCreate with the parameterized emptyRow face and no text hook (honest minimal face).

legalDomain.conditionalEmission: The artifact exists per view only when judged applyEvents are nonEmpty; multi is one kernel file per view with multiple event functions. Single-project base is 0 files. The kernel class name is the view name plus ApplyEvent, in the projection package plus .handlers — never doubled.
legalDomain.judgedInput: The generator consumes already-judged applyEvents: per event {eventName, eventFqn, applyForm in {create, updateOnly, delete, persistenceIdCreate}, bodyExpr final form, deletePairs (exactly two for delete), viewColumns}. Empty/???/unknown-dialect events (raw degraded) never reach the target file; duplicates are rejected; a persistenceId view rejects plain create-form events; delete requires exactly two judged pairs. Fail-closed (D-P08).
legalDomain.semanticsFace: Per view the generator emits a semantics trait in the handlers package declaring exactly the hooks that view's functions need (StockLedgerApplyEventSemantics: emptyRow / stamped / text; StockLedgerSnapshotApplyEventSemantics: emptyRow(entityId, tenantId) / stamped — no text hook, honest minimal face). The handwritten impl (infrastructure.projection, isolation zone, @Singleton, never emitted or overwritten by the generator) owns the business defaults: the empty row (all columns, business-owned — the raw eight-type derivation table dissolves), the named untimestamped default (epoch0/null -> now; the view's single sanctioned clock read, at a fixed named location, never inline getOrElse(now())), and the text default (null -> empty). The bootstrap module (infrastructure.bootstrap, generated) binds each face to its impl with an explicit Guice binding.
legalDomain.importFace: Kernel imports: javax.inject.{Inject, Singleton}, then the configured business-base table view import (the raw hardcoded net.imadz.metarch prefix is an explicit correction, never emitted), then event imports distinct in judged first-occurrence order. The semantics traits need no import of kernel symbols (same package). Kernel files carry zero java.* import statements; java.time.Instant appears only as fully-qualified type references in the faces.
legalDomain.functionForms: create: def on<E>(existing: Option[View], e: E): View = existing.getOrElse(sem.emptyRow).copy(...). updateOnly: def on<E>(row: View, e: E): View = row.copy(...). delete: def on<E>(e: E): (String, String) = (key0, key1) from the two judged deletePairs. persistenceIdCreate: def on<E>(e: E, entityId: String): View = sem.emptyRow(entityId, ...).copy(...). One doc line per function in the raw doc style. Functions follow judged order.
legalDomain.kernelZeroMechanism: The kernel classes carry @Singleton @Inject() with only the semantics face as constructor parameter (same package, no import); no repository call, no ActorRef, no PB, no ViewMachine reference, no MANUAL zone, no ???, no clock read, no Id reference, no default-literal semantics — pinned structurally. The kernel-local upsertBy helper is pure list mechanics, not business semantics.
legalDomain.supplyContract: Supplied files are handwritten and never emitted by the generator: the two semantics impls (infrastructure.projection isolation zone), the sealed ReservationEvent entity family (domain; CreditBalanceEntity precedent), the two Table objects with view case classes and column inventories (shell repository contract), and the trimmed net.imadz.common.Id common supply (alias + deterministic of; random face excluded).
legalDomain.layout: Emission holds a 100-column discipline: emptyRow and copy argument lists render one named argument per line (opening paren on the def or body-head line when it fits, closing paren at the statement indent); module bindings wrap at the .to(...) call; def parameter lists wrap one parameter per line over the limit; imports are exempt; no non-import app line exceeds 100 characters (structural property).

decisions.choice: RATIFIED DIRECTION (2026-11-20 walkthrough): the judged input contract is fail-closed — only executable events with applyForm in {create, updateOnly, delete, persistenceIdCreate} reach the file; degraded events are rejected at validation; delete requires exactly two judged pairs; duplicate event names are rejected; a persistenceId view rejects plain create-form events. The derivability clause (bare-Instant/non-derivable column rejection) is superseded by the semantics-face ownership: the impl may default any column. The rejection guards are enforced at the generator phase (FORMAL_INPUT negatives); the golden shows the admitted shapes.

RATIFIED DIRECTION (D1 None patch = clears the column, executable demonstration = onLedgerReopened settledAt = None). Timestamp semantics moved behind the semantics face per the user's 2026-11-20 ruling: epoch0/null -> the NAMED untimestamped default (now) inside the handwritten impl — never an inline .getOrElse(java.time.Instant.now()) patch; kernel behavior properties run against a deterministic stub semantics (stamped = Option(raw) passthrough, emptyRow = zero-UUID row, text = identity); the impl's own clock semantics are properties on the impl face.

RATIFIED DIRECTION: the first kernel import uses the configured business base; kernel zero-mechanism pinned structurally (now including: no clock read, no Id reference, no default-literal semantics inlined — all delegated through the injected face); the shell ViewMachine contract stays out of this sample; viewColumns carry the original resolved signature.

RATIFIED (2026-11-20 user proposal, V1 class injection): per-view business-semantics traits are generated (the face), handwritten impls live in the infrastructure.projection isolation zone and are never created or overwritten by the generator (sha-registered supplies), and the bootstrap module binds face to impl — the same face/impl/assembly structure as the approved toolgate families. This dissolves the raw eight-type default derivation table, the derivability degradation, and the inline ts/strOr template idioms into business-owned named methods. Rationale recorded: defaults, missing-timestamp meaning and null-text meaning are business decisions, not generator logic; the impl is rewritable without regeneration; tests stub the face for deterministic kernel behavior.

RATIFIED (2026-11-20, after a live scalameta 4.7.7 probe showed named arguments and assignment targets parse to the same Term.Assign node): the Term.Assign violation is judged by CONTEXT, not by layer — a named argument always sits in an argument clause (Term.ArgClause parent; probe evidence: copy/new named args parent = Term.ArgClause, statement assignment parent = Term.Block) so it is admitted in BOTH layers, while Term.Assign in any other position is a real assignment target and is a violation in BOTH layers; Defn.Var stays banned in both layers. This replaces the earlier layer-based admission (E2a), which left a latent domain-layer false positive. argumentClause is a one-decision named predicate (measured cc=1); forbidden measures cc=17 with the exact exception row updated.

RATIFIED SCOPE: the Instant/UUID boundary term-name admission exists ONLY for the handwritten supply files that need it (the two semantics impls read the clock once each through the named untimestamped default; the common Id supply parses UUID.fromString); the generated kernel files inline none of them — pinned by the clock-confinement and identity-confinement structural properties. Random, Clock, LocalDateTime, Date, Await stay banned in both layers; randomUUID is pinned absent from all app sources.

Pure case-class files register zero measured scopes, which the gate requires nonempty: Table objects carry their column inventory as a val, and the entity events carry constructor require guards per the established curated domain discipline. The net.imadz.common supply and the infrastructure impls/module are classified boundary.

RATIFIED (C2): the target emission layout holds a 100-column discipline — emptyRow and copy argument lists render one named argument per line, module bindings wrap at the .to(...) call, def parameter lists wrap over the limit, imports are exempt, and no non-import app line exceeds 100 characters (structural property). Replaces the raw template's single-line argument emission.

RATIFIED: the nominal event supply follows the real-source entity idiom (CreditBalanceEntity precedent): a sealed ReservationEvent family with every event extending it. Supply-fidelity only — this family imports events by eventFqn and never emits event types.
